hub.meta_title: Letting agents in Durham | Hello New Home
hub.meta_description: Durham letting agents: 12% full management, no VAT, no extras, no lock-in. A Local Partner on the ground and the selective licence handled for you.
hub.intro: Hello New Home covers Durham City, Chester-le-Street, Consett, Stanley, Bishop Auckland, Newton Aycliffe and the villages between, across the DH and County Durham DL postcodes. Our Local Partner lives here and does the viewings, inspections and check-ins. Contracts, Right to Rent checks, deposits, rent collection and the Renters' Rights Act paperwork run from our head office. Full management is 12% of the rent with no VAT, no extras and no lock-in, and at County Durham rents that is the whole fee.

sections.html:
Three things bring Durham landlords to us. A letter from Durham County Council about a selective licence, with a form that asks for certificates they cannot find. The Renters' Rights Act, which rewrote the tenancy they signed years ago on 1 May 2026. And an agent in Durham City or Chester-le-Street who takes a week to call back and holds them to a 12-month agreement.

Our answer is 12% of the rent, no VAT added, no renewal, inspection or notice fees, and 30 days' notice to leave. The licence application, the written statement of terms and the landlord database registration are part of management. And the person who inspects your house lives in the county.

sections.h2: Durham rents and what 12% costs here
sections.html:
The ONS average private rent for County Durham was £650 a month in August 2026, up 6.1% on the year from £612. The North East average was £788. At £650 our fee is £78 a month.

Our £150 cap only bites at rents of £1,250 or more, which in County Durham means a Durham City four-bed near the Viaduct or a large house in Belmont. So the honest description of our fee here is not the cap but the absence of everything else: 12%, no VAT, no extras.

A county average covers Consett terraces and Durham City townhouses alike. The free rent review prices your house against lets on your street this month.

sections.h2: Selective licensing, mandatory HMO licensing and the new Article 4
sections.html:
Durham County Council's selective licensing scheme runs from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2027 and covers 103 of the county's 324 neighbourhoods, roughly 42% of its private rented homes. Inside a designated area every privately rented house needs a licence, whoever the tenant is. A successor scheme from 1 April 2027 was consulted on in summer 2026 and the outcome is awaited.

We check every address against the council's map before marketing, complete the application and put the expiry on your calendar. Mandatory HMO licensing applies to five or more people from two or more households.

Shared houses changed in August 2026 too. The council confirmed a countywide Article 4 direction from 17 August 2026, so a new small HMO of three to six people needs planning permission across the county, not only in Durham City, Belmont, Newton Hall and the areas already covered. If you let by the room, hellomyroom, our shared-house team, manages planning, licence and fire safety together.

sections.h2: The streets and who rents them
sections.html:
• Durham City and the Viaduct: Durham University had 20,887 students in 2024/25, plus staff at the university and University Hospital of North Durham. The strongest short-stay market in the county.
  • Gilesgate and Belmont: student and professional shared houses, family long lets, and the parts of the city where Article 4 planning control on HMOs already applied.
  • Chester-le-Street: commuters to Newcastle on long lets, at rents close to the county average.
  • Consett and Stanley: family lets in the north-west of the county, where 12% of rent is a small monthly figure.
  • Bishop Auckland: long lets to local workers and families, with the market town as the draw.
  • Newton Aycliffe: Aycliffe Business Park is the county's largest employment site, with around 500 companies anchored by Hitachi Rail and Gestamp, and a warehouse completed in 2025 added more than 1,100 jobs. Demand is working families and contractors.

sections.h2: How the Local Partner model works in Durham
sections.html:
Our Local Partner is the face of Hello New Home in County Durham: photographs, viewings, move-ins, quarterly inspections and the handover when you switch from another agent. They never hold your money.

Everything regulated runs from head office: the agreement and written statement of terms, Right to Rent checks, deposit protection, rent collection, the repairs desk, the compliance calendar and the licence application. We belong to a redress scheme and a client money protection scheme, both named on our fee sheet, and your agreement is with Hello New Home.

If you know your patch and want to open the next town, the Local Partner programme explains how.

Ask for a free rent review. Send the address and we call within one working day with a realistic rent for your street, the selective licensing position for the address, and a written comparison of our 12% against what you pay now. If you own a flat near the cathedral, ask for the free short-let appraisal and you get both figures side by side. Our Local Partner will bring either to you in person.

faqs.q: Does my Durham property need a selective licence?
faqs.a: If it is inside one of Durham County Council's designated areas, yes, whatever the size of the property or the type of tenant. The current scheme runs to 31 March 2027 and a successor has been consulted on. We check your address against the council's map and complete the application.

faqs.q: What does full management cost in Durham?
faqs.a: 12% of the monthly rent with no VAT added and no extras. On the County Durham average rent of £650 that is £78 a month. The fee is capped at £150, which only applies above £1,250 a month. Tenant Find on its own is £495, no let no fee.

faqs.q: Who looks after my property day to day?
faqs.a: Our Local Partner in County Durham does the viewings, quarterly inspections, move-ins and move-outs. Contracts, deposits, rent collection and compliance run from head office. The Local Partner never holds your money, and the agreement is with Hello New Home.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a shared house in County Durham?
faqs.a: Durham County Council confirmed a countywide Article 4 direction taking effect from 17 August 2026, so a new small HMO of three to six people needs planning permission anywhere in the county. Larger HMOs always did. Our shared-house team, hellomyroom, checks the position before you let by the room.

faqs.q: What changed for Durham landlords on 1 May 2026?
faqs.a: The Renters' Rights Act came into force in England. Tenancies are periodic, section 21 has gone, rent can rise once a year by notice, and a written statement of terms is required before the tenancy starts. The landlord database opens from December 2026. We handle all of it.

sections.h2: The Renters' Rights Act, done for you
sections.html:
Since 1 May 2026 every tenancy in England is periodic. Fixed terms are gone, section 21 is gone, and possession runs on the Section 8 grounds. Rent can go up once in any 12 months by a Section 13 notice with two months' notice, and the tenant can take it to the tribunal. You cannot take more than one month's rent in advance, and a tenant's request to keep a pet needs an answer within 28 days.

Before any tenancy starts the tenant must have a written statement of the key terms; missing it carries a fine of up to £7,000. We serve it with the agreement. From December 2026 the private rented sector database opens and every landlord in England will need to register; we complete your entry when your region's window opens.

If you ever need the house back to live in or to sell, Grounds 1 and 1A need four months' notice and cannot be used in the first 12 months of a tenancy. We tell you the earliest real date rather than the one you were hoping for.

Your tenant does not need to move for you to. We give notice to your current agent, collect the deposit certificate, the certificates and the licence, check the file against the Act and the council's licensing map, and our Local Partner meets the tenant at the house. If a gas certificate has lapsed or the written statement was never served, you hear about it before we take over, not after.

sections.html: Fill in the free rent review with the address and, if you have one, your current agent's fee. Within one working day you get a realistic rent for your street, the selective licence position for the address and a written fee comparison. No obligation, and our Local Partner can come to the house if you would like a second opinion in person.

faqs.q: Is the 12% fee really the whole cost?
faqs.a: Yes. 12% of the monthly rent, no VAT, no renewal, inspection or notice fees. The council's selective licence fee is a council charge and is separate from our fee. On a £650 rent you pay £78 a month.

faqs.q: Do you do Right to Rent checks?
faqs.a: Yes. Every adult who will live in the property is checked before the tenancy starts, as England requires. Head office runs the check and keeps the record; our Local Partner collects the documents in person where that is easier for the tenant.

faqs.q: Can I still get my property back if I need it?
faqs.a: Yes, on the grounds the Renters' Rights Act allows. If you or close family need to move in, or you want to sell, Grounds 1 and 1A need four months' notice and cannot be used in the first 12 months. We advise on timing before you decide.

faqs.q: Who applies for the selective licence?
faqs.a: We do, as part of management. We check the address against Durham County Council's designated areas, prepare the application with the certificates it needs and put the expiry date on your compliance calendar. The council's licence fee is paid to the council.

faqs.q: How quickly can you take over a managed property?
faqs.a: Usually within the notice period you have with your current agent. We handle the notice, the deposit and file transfer and the paperwork check, and our Local Partner introduces themselves to the tenant. Tell us your agent's notice period and we work to it.

shortlets.meta_title: Airbnb & short-let management Durham | Hello New Home
shortlets.meta_description: Short-let management in Durham: 18% of net booking revenue, no 90-night cap, the night test and council tax premium explained, and a free appraisal first.
shortlets.h1: Airbnb and short-let management in Durham
shortlets.intro: Durham has a real short-stay market and a real quiet season, and an honest appraisal shows both. We run long lets and short lets in the county from the same team, so we can tell you what your flat near the cathedral nets as a short let and what it nets as a tenancy, after every cost, using Durham occupancy rather than a national average. Full SA Management is 18% of net booking revenue. There is no 90-night cap outside London.

sections.h2: What drives short stays in Durham
sections.html:
County Durham recorded 21.98 million visits in 2025, with 1.67 million of them staying visitors, and Durham Cathedral alone had 393,090 visitors in 2024 and reported record numbers in 2025. Add the university's open days, graduations and term-start weekends, hospital and contractor stays, and the Lumiere weekends, and Durham City has demand most northern cities would envy.

It also has a thin January, and a flat in Newton Aycliffe or Consett will not book like one on the peninsula. Our appraisal is built on Durham City occupancy by month, and if your address is in the wrong part of the county for short stays we tell you and quote the long let instead.

Full SA Management is 18% of net booking revenue, with cleaning passed through at cost. It covers dynamic pricing, guest vetting and messaging around the clock, cleaning and linen coordination, restocking, repairs, review management, a monthly owner statement and the night-count tracker. SA Co-Host is 12% for owners who want pricing, the listing and guest messages handled but will run their own cleaner. SA Launch is £495 for photography, listings on Airbnb, Booking.com and a direct-booking page, pricing rules, a house manual and the compliance pack, and is waived with 12 months of Full SA Management. No VAT is added, and you can leave on 30 days' notice.

sections.h2: The rules for a short let in County Durham
sections.html:
Planning. There is no 90-night limit outside Greater London. A proposed short-let use class for England has been announced but not legislated, so for now a change of use is judged case by case. We note the position for your address in the appraisal.

Business rates or council tax. In England a self-catering property is rated as a business only if it was available to let for 140 nights and actually let for 70 nights in the past year. Below that it pays council tax, and since 1 April 2025 Durham County Council charges a 100% premium on second homes, which means double council tax for a short let that misses the test. The tracker shows you the count each month.

The register. The government has said a national short-let register for England will be running by March 2027. We will register your property when it opens.

Safety. Fire risk assessment, gas and electrical certificates, PAT testing and an insurance check are in the SA Launch compliance pack. This is the list we work to, not legal advice.

If a short let in Durham City should become a tenancy in September, or a long let in Gilesgate should try the summer as short stays, Flex Switch moves it with the same agent, the same owner statement and no re-onboarding. A national co-host cannot take a property back as a long let; a high-street agent will not run it as a short let. We do both, and our Local Partner is the one who meets the cleaner, checks the changeover and answers the door.

sections.h2: Next step: the free short-let appraisal
sections.html: Request the free short-let appraisal with your address. You get the long-let figure and the short-let figure side by side, net of platform fees, cleaning, utilities, voids and management, plus the planning, night-test and council tax position for the property in writing. If the long let wins, the figure is the same one you would get from the free rent review, and we manage it at 12%.

faqs.q: Is there a 90-night limit on short lets in Durham?
faqs.a: No. The 90-night rule applies only in Greater London. Outside London there is no fixed night limit, and whether a short let is a change of use is judged case by case. We note the planning position for your address in the free appraisal.

faqs.q: Will my Durham short let pay business rates or council tax?
faqs.a: Business rates only if it was available for 140 nights and actually let for 70 in the past year. Otherwise council tax applies, and Durham County Council has charged a 100% premium on second homes since 1 April 2025. Our tracker reports your night count monthly.

faqs.q: How much do you charge to manage a short let in Durham?
faqs.a: Full SA Management is 18% of net booking revenue, cleaning at cost. SA Co-Host is 12%. SA Launch is £495, waived with 12 months of Full SA Management. No VAT is added and there is no 12-month minimum.

faqs.q: Which parts of County Durham suit short stays?
faqs.a: Durham City first, for the cathedral, the university and the hospital. Chester-le-Street and Bishop Auckland can work for contractor stays. Most of the county's towns and villages earn more as long lets, and the appraisal will say so if that is true of yours.

faqs.q: Can I switch between short let and long let?
faqs.a: Yes. Flex Switch is included: a property can move between short let and tenancy with us and no re-onboarding. A 90-night-plus let or a tenancy is managed under the long-let fee, and the owner statement stays the same.
